newsitem.title: USA: Financial giants need coordinated oversight - report.
newsitem.headline: Financial giants need coordinated oversight - report.

text.p: Financial regulators around the globe need to work together to craft a supervisory system that better reflects the blurring lines between banking, securities and insurance industries, a group said Thursday.

The increasingly global nature of markets also calls for better coordination among national regulators of financial institutions, the Institute of International Finance said in a report prepared by a task force of its large members.

"The regulatory system for certain firms will need to evolve from today's largely national basis with diverse supervisors responsible for various segments of the financial industry," said Charles Dallara, IIF managing director.
The report stressed that the new regulatory framework should apply only to a limited number of "globally active" firms and not affect such institutions as retail banks or small insurance firms.
Improved information-sharing procedures among regulatory agencies and across various sectors could mark a first step toward adapting current methods of overseeing global markets.
But the group said bigger changes are also needed.
The report advocated a "risk-based" approach toward regulation, with an initial focus on collecting information on common risks present in the financial arena.
"Supervisors would have to agree among themselves on the core risks that financial firms in all jurisdictions must be able to manage," the report said.
It also called on financial firms to expand their public disclosure to enable regulators and other parties to better understand their various approaches to risk management.

Adopting a risk-based approach to regulatory reporting could reduce overlapping and sometimes contradictory reporting requirements that apply to firms doing business in many locations, a key goal of many large financial institutions.
"This is going to be an evolutionary process," Dallara said. "These changes will not take place overnight but it's important that they be advanced."
The group's report concluded that both supervisors and financial firms "share the same overriding goal: to promote the safety and soundness of the global financial system."
